statement: On the new-customer source path, local Mongo customer save occurs before the PSP client call. A later PSP/client/response failure can leave that local state; relation persistence happens in a later save. A distributed atomic transaction or exactly-once creation is not established.
assumptions: Source advice invokes body rather than serving cache
Earlier checks and local calls reach the stated source path

statement: The update source saves the customer before checking for any PSP relation, then calls the client for each relation. It can raise the source 404 after save or fail part way through remote updates; earlier local/remote state is not shown to roll back.
assumptions: Source reaches the update body
No unexamined middleware supplies a wider transaction

statement: RequestHashCacheKeyResolver sorts object properties/maps, serializes payload, joins method + newline + URI + newline + JSON, then Base64-encodes input.getBytes(). Missing request uses random UUID; serialization failure uses method/URI/payload.hashCode. Cache and lock expressions evaluate the resolver independently, so fallback keys need not match. This is the logical resolver value, not a verified full physical Redis key.
assumptions: Source key-construction association; module/version/charset and physical cache-prefix enforcement remain bounded
This is a source declaration/association, not proof of effective wire acceptance or deployed policy
